s1.syndrome_frame: Right upper abdominal pain with mass and abnormal liver function
salient_findings: Heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa
key_facts: 2-month history of right upper abdominal pain
No nausea, vomiting, chills, or fever
Right upper abdominal tenderness without rebound or palpable masses
Negative Murphy’s sign and shifting dullness
Ultrasonography showed heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa
Contrast-enhanced CT showed lesion in the right hepatic lobe and multiple enlarged hepatic hilar lymph nodes

shortlist.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CA19-9 and imaging findings of a heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa

shortlist.label: Gallbladder cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Gallstones, gallbladder wall thickening, and a mass near the gallbladder fossa

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated AFP and a lesion in the right hepatic lobe

shortlist.label: Cholangiocarcinoma of the gallbladder
shortlist.why_kept: Gallstones, gallbladder wall thickening, and a mass near the gallbladder fossa

shortlist.label: Hepatic metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CEA and multiple enlarged hepatic hilar lymph nodes

raw.rationale: Elevated CA19-9 level, presence of a heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa, and intrahepatic bile duct dilatation on liver MRI are consistent with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma

rejected.label: Gallbladder cancer
rejected.why: No palpable masses and negative Murphy’s sign make gallbladder cancer less likely

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: Normal AFP level and absence of hepatosplenomegaly or cirrhosis make hepatocellular carcinoma less likely

rejected.label: Cholangiocarcinoma of the gallbladder
rejected.why: Imaging studies suggest the lesion is in the liver, not the gallbladder

rejected.label: Hepatic metastasis
rejected.why: No extrahepatic primary tumor was identified, making hepatic metastasis less likely
